planNote: Verify all four witnesses with core geometric and visual checks, run full suite and PRT checks, and probe contested/timing-dependent claims for Witnesses A and B with speed and time sensitivity sweeps.

report.headline: All 22 independent verification jobs completed with 0 failures and 100% agreement across all 17 machine-compared metrics against world sha 526ea902d593, confirming the obstruction of Witnesses B and D and the clear sightlines of Witnesses A, C, and both drivers.
agreements: Job full_suite independently reproduced all 10/10 baseline timing, kinematic plausibility, and sightline checks with zero code drift between local and public repo checks.

Jobs sl_wit_A, rob_wit_A, gaze_wit_A, and r_wit_A reproduced Witness A's unobstructed view of veh_A at t=4.5s (466.79 m distance, 0/25 robustness samples blocked, 2.8° off-axis gaze, and 2,533/2,533 visible target pixels after cab filtering), confirming F2.

Jobs sl_wit_B, rob_wit_B, gaze_wit_B, and r_wit_B reproduced the blockage of Witness B's sightline to veh_A by veh_T_tractor at t=9.8s (30.22 m distance, 21/25 robustness samples blocked, 31.5° off-axis gaze, and 0/3,426 visible pixels), confirming F1.

Jobs sl_wit_C, rob_wit_C, gaze_wit_C, and r_wit_C reproduced Witness C's clear sightline to veh_T_trailer at impact t=10.43s (32.53 m distance, 0/25 robustness samples blocked, 7.0° off-axis gaze, and 4,048/4,092 or 98.9% visible pixels), confirming F4.

Jobs sl_wit_D, rob_wit_D, gaze_wit_D, and r_wit_D reproduced Witness D's complete obstruction toward veh_A at t=10.43s (33.25 m distance, 25/25 robustness samples blocked, 1.2° off-axis gaze, and 0/4,747 visible pixels), confirming F3.

Job prt_all independently confirmed F5, showing both drivers (veh_A to veh_T_trailer and veh_T_tractor to veh_A) had a continuous 10.43 s unobstructed line of sight from t=0.00s to t=10.43s, exceeding the 1.0–2.5 s perception-reaction time range.
disagreements: Blocker ID label on Witness D (sl_wit_D vs local checks and r_wit_D): sl_wit_D reports the primary raycast blocker as bld_store at 33.25 m, whereas local checks and r_wit_D report occ_store_front (3,426/3,426 pixels blocked by occ_store_front). Job rob_wit_D shows both co-located meshes block the sightline across the 25-sample grid (22 by bld_store, 3 by occ_store_front), indicating co-planar geometry ordering between the store building and storefront occluder rather than a disagreement on visibility (0/101 steps visible).

Witness A trailer-occlusion timing (wt_wit_A vs local claim text): Witness A claimed the turning trailer eventually blocked his view of the car, and wt_wit_A tested t=2.5s to 6.5s expecting to capture the cutoff; however, veh_A remained visible across the entire 2.5–6.5s sweep (400.8 m to 532.81 m), with sl_wit_A showing visibility in 93/101 timeline steps (indicating the 8 blocked steps occur after t=6.5s).

Raw pixel self-occlusion in render jobs (r_wit_A, r_wit_C): r_wit_A and r_wit_C report rawVisibleFraction=0 due to 100% raw pixel blockage by the witnesses' own vehicle meshes (veh_witA and veh_witC), whereas the observer-filtered visibleFraction is 1.0 (100%) and 0.989 (98.9%), respectively—a known modeling artifact documented in F2.
sensitivities: Witness A (rob_wit_A, wt_wit_A, gaze_wit_A): Highly robust; 0/25 samples blocked across all perturbation rings from 0.5 m to 8 m, central gaze at 2.8° off-axis (73.06° if looking at mark_pole_poi), and continuously visible across the entire ±2.0 s time sweep (t=2.5s to 6.5s).

Witness B position and gaze (rob_wit_B, gaze_wit_B): At t=9.8s, Witness B is completely blocked (25/25) within 0.5 m and 1.0 m perturbation rings; partial visibility only begins at a ≥2 m shift (21/25 blocked at 2 m: 11 by veh_T_tractor, 10 by occ_shelter; 19/25 at 3 m; 17/25 at 5–8 m). Furthermore, veh_A is 31.5° off-axis (peripheral) assuming gaze at mark_poi.

Witness B time and speed (wt_wit_B, ws_wit_B): Witness B's sightline is clear from t=7.8s to 9.3s, but becomes blocked right before impact at t=9.8s by veh_T_tractor and at t=10.3s–10.8s by occ_shelter (only clearing post-impact at t=11.3s). In speed sweeps (ws_wit_B), the sightline at t=9.8s remains blocked for speed multipliers k=0.7 to 1.1 (17/25 to 25/25 blocked) and only clears the center ray if veh_A approaches at least 20% faster (k=1.2 or 1.3, where 10/25 and 9/25 samples still remain blocked).

Witness C (rob_wit_C, gaze_wit_C): Highly robust; 0/25 samples blocked across all perturbation rings from 0.5 m to 8 m, with a central gaze angle of 7.0° off-axis (98.9% of trailer pixels visible at impact, with 1.1% occluded by colliding veh_A).

Witness D (rob_wit_D, sl_wit_D, gaze_wit_D): Completely invariant to perturbation; 25/25 samples are blocked across every ring from 0.5 m to 8 m and 0/101 timeline steps are visible, despite a direct 1.2° gaze alignment toward the impact point.

finding_updates.note: Confirmed by sl_wit_B, r_wit_B (0/3,426 visible pixels), rob_wit_B (25/25 blocked within 1 m, 21/25 at 2 m), wt_wit_B (blocked from t=9.8s through impact at 10.43s by tractor and shelter), and ws_wit_B (blocked unless veh_A speed increases by ≥20%).

Confirmed by r_wit_A, which explicitly captures the rawBlockers veh_witA fraction=1.0 self-occlusion vs 100% (2,533/2,533 px) clear visibility once the cab mesh is excluded, alongside sl_wit_A and rob_wit_A (0/25 blocked across 0.5–8 m).

Confirmed by sl_wit_D (0/101 timeline steps visible), r_wit_D (0/4,747 visible pixels, 100% blocked by occ_store_front), and rob_wit_D (25/25 blocked across all rings up to 8 m by bld_store and occ_store_front).
Confirmed by sl_wit_C (visible at t=10.43s at 32.53 m), rob_wit_C (0/25 blocked across 0.5–8 m rings), gaze_wit_C (7.0° off-axis), and r_wit_C (4,048/4,092 pixels or 98.9% visible).
Confirmed by full_suite (all timing and plausibility checks pass) and prt_all (10.43 s continuous unobstructed sightline for both veh_A and veh_T_tractor drivers from t=0.00s to impact).
No sandbox jobs directly tested solar angles or weather documentation, though scene renders (r_overhead, r_wit_A..D) executed cleanly against the world file.

jobs.interpretation: The reconstruction verifies that vehicle kinematics and timings are physically plausible, with clear sightlines confirmed for witnesses A and C, while the views of witnesses B and D were obstructed by a tractor and a building.
Both drivers had an unobstructed line of sight for 10.43 seconds prior to impact, providing sufficient perception-reaction time.
Witness wit_A had an unobstructed line of sight to vehicle veh_A at the 4.5-second mark across a distance of approximately 467 meters.
Witness wit_A had a completely unobstructed line of sight to vehicle veh_A with zero blocked samples across all tested perturbation radii.
Witness wit_A had vehicle veh_A directly in their central field of view with a gaze angle only 2.8 degrees off-axis at observation time 4.5 seconds.
Witness wit_A had a clear, unobstructed view of vehicle veh_A across the entire time sweep from 2.5 to 6.5 seconds.
At the observation time of 9.8 seconds, witness wit_B did not have a clear line of sight to veh_A because it was blocked by veh_T_tractor.
Witness wit_B's line of sight to vehicle veh_A at time 9.8s was largely obstructed by the tractor and shelter, resulting in a partial verdict with 21 out of 25 sightlines blocked.
The result indicates that witness wit_B had vehicle veh_A in their peripheral line of sight at approximately 31.5 degrees off-axis at observation time 9.8 seconds.
Witness B could not have seen vehicle A at the baseline speed because their line of sight was blocked by the tractor, and vehicle A only becomes visible if it was traveling at least 20% faster.
Witness B's line of sight to vehicle A was obstructed by veh_T_tractor at the observation time of 9.8 seconds.
Witness wit_C had an unobstructed view of the target trailer at the observation time of 10.43 seconds.
Witness wit_C had an unobstructed line of sight to veh_T_trailer at t=10.43s with zero blocked samples across all tested perturbation radii.
Witness wit_C had the trailer (veh_T_trailer) well within their central field of view at t=10.43s with an off-axis gaze angle of approximately 7 degrees.
Witness wit_D could not see vehicle veh_A at any point because their sightline was completely obstructed by bld_store.
Witness wit_D's line of sight to vehicle veh_A at time 10.43 was robustly blocked by the store building and store front across all sampled positions and radii.
Witness wit_D had vehicle A directly within their line of sight at 10.43 seconds with an off-axis gaze angle of 1.2 degrees.
The overhead view rendered 51 frames successfully with 8 out of 10 verification checks passing.
The simulation confirms that witness A had an unobstructed line of sight to vehicle A at the 4.5-second observation mark.
Witness B did not have an unobstructed view of vehicle A as claimed, because their line of sight was blocked by a tractor at the critical observation time.
Witness C had a clear, unobstructed line of sight to the truck trailer at the time of the collision, corroborating their account.
Witness D's line of sight to the vehicle was completely blocked by the storefront at the time of observation, corroborating their statement that they could not see the highway.
